positions.name: MigrationDecisionRecord
positions.frame: how does the migration decision itself get expressed — as a live declarative act versus a recorded summary label?
positions.why: src-1 performs the decision in prose, present-progressive and decisive ('We're switching from PostgreSQL to QuantumDB'); src-3 restates the same content as a bolded, arrow-notation summary heading ('Database migration: PostgreSQL → QuantumDB'). Both the conviction and relational reads mark these two as decision-grade/authority-ranking rather than mere claims — the same settled move surfaces once in narrative form and once in structured recap form, which is the read this group holds.

positions.name: PerformanceCostJustification
positions.frame: what is offered as the performance/cost rationale for the switch, across its narrative and summary forms?
positions.why: src-2 states the justification in prose as a flat, unhedged pair of benefits ('10x query performance, lower licensing cost'); src-4 restates the performance half alone as a bolded summary bullet ('10x analytical queries'). Both directional passes mark these claim-grade (not decision-grade) and market-pricing/rational-persuasion in register — the rationale is offered as evidence, not ratified. Held in tension: the summary form (src-4) drops the licensing-cost half present in the narrative form (src-2), a narrowing this group surfaces without resolving.
